newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CFTC to propose lifting ban on ag options.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CFTC to propose lifting ban on ag options.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission staff released a study on Wednesday that proposes a formal rulemaking to lift the longstanding ban on agricultural trade options.
"I expect advance notice of a proposed rulemaking will appear in the Federal Register in a short time period," said Paul Architzel, chief counsel of the CFTC's Division of Economic Analysis.
He said the rulemaking could begin in the next 30 days.

A so-called white paper released by the CFTC staff recommended that the agency also clarify the definition for swap agreement exemptions, and to reissue an agency interpretation of agricultural forward contracts.
Both actions are necessary in permitting the trading of off-exchange agricultural trade options, the report said.

Architzel said the agency's analysis showed there was great interest among farmers, elevators and other producers in using ag trade options, especially because of last year's farm bill that eliminated most government support programs.
The CFTC report also noted that ag trade options could bring the potential for a higher risk of fraud, as well as credit and liquidity risks.
